newsitem.title: USA: Texas to continue tobacco trial preparations.
newsitem.headline: Texas to continue tobacco trial preparations.

text.p: Texas trial lawyers will continue working on a state lawsuit against the tobacco industry until a settlement reached on Friday is ratified in Congress, Texas Attorney General Dan Morales said.

"I have instructed our lawyers to continue with trial preparations," he said. "I am hopeful that Congress will ratify this agreement...(but) in this business, you just never know when something like this moves into the political arena."
Morales would not speculate on the possibility that a hard-won settlement carved out between state attorneys general and the tobacco industry could unravel on Capitol Hill.
"There are those opposed to the agreement, and those that like the status quo," he said. "Suffice it to say, (industry lobbyists) will be active in Congress in the coming months.

Texas in March 1996 filed the largest of the 40 state lawsuits against the tobacco industry, seeking $14 billion in damages to cover state and federal costs of health care for indigent smokers, Morales said.

The state expects to recover $5 billion from the landmark agreement that requires tobacco companies to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years to compensate states and smokers and pledged to reduce smoking by teen-agers.
"Texas can now say goodbye to Joe Camel and the Marlboro Man," he said, referring to advertising icons of R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co and Philip Morris Cos Inc, respectively.
Morales said tobacco companies should boost domestic cigarette prices to recover the costs of the settlement instead of working to boost sales and profits overseas.

Morales said the tobacco companies agreed to a negotiated settlement to avoid potentially larger costs of losing the state lawsuits. "We were going to win our trial and we were going to win it big," he said.
